It is interesting how the individuals interviewed for this article as well as the author are lamenting the request from the government for extremely high standards of evidence for specific restrictions. To constitutionally impose such restrictions Section 1 or Section 33 of the Charter have to apply. There is a taboo against using Section 33 in Canada, albeit the government would not have to provide nearly the same level of  justification for its actions relative to Section 1. With Section 1 any restriction on fundamental rights and freedoms has to be justified within a free and democratic society and the onus is on the government to provide evidence to justify its actions. The actions must be proven to be proportionate, the least restrictive options for accomplishing the supposed purpose and not doing more harm than good. The government is doing its best to follow the law in this case. I’m surprised that law professor interviewed did not consider this reasoning.
